ITQAN:v3p107/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p107/r7.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p107/r7.claim: A feminine is grammatically masculine when construed by a masculine equivalent: admonition, place, sun or rising body, or the meaning of raḥma; al-Jawharī explains قريب by construing it with iḥsān.
ITQAN:v3p107/r7.anchor: ومنها تذكير المؤنث على تأويله بمذكر نحو ﴿ فمن جاءه موعظة من ربه ﴾ أي وعظ

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p531#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p531#2/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p531#2/r3.claim: Most readers lighten ميتا, while Abū Jaʿfar and Khālid double the yāʾ; the resurrection of people is likened to reviving a dead land.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p531#2/r3.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: ميتا بالتخفيف وأبو جعفر، وخالد: بالتثقيل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p531#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p531#2/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p531#2/r5.claim: The vegetation examples distinguish yearly picked produce whose plant remains, crops sown for one or two years, and mixed kinds; crops are mostly food while fruits are largely treats and sometimes food.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p531#2/r5.anchor: ونبه فيما تعلق به الإنبات على ما يقطف كل سنة ويبقى أصله

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p434/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p434/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p434/r2.claim: Heaven and earth provide signs for resurrection, reward and punishment, and monotheism by showing God’s power, wisdom, and provision; they warn the humble who turn to Him.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p434/r2.anchor: A reference is made to the signs of the heavens and the earth which if benefited from bear evidence to the Day of Judgement

NAHHAS:v4p221/r15.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p221/r15.speaker: أبو إسحاق
NAHHAS:v4p221/r15.claim: Abu Ishaq parses rizqan as either a verbal noun or an object of purpose.
NAHHAS:v4p221/r15.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق رزقا مصدر ويجوز أن يكون مفعولا من أجله

NAHHAS:v4p221/r16.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p221/r16.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p221/r16.claim: The revived town is barren, without crops or vegetation.
NAHHAS:v4p221/r16.anchor: أي مجدبة ليس فيها زرع ولا نبات

NAHHAS:v4p221/r17.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p221/r17.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p221/r17.claim: Kadhālika al-khurūj is a subject-predicate clause; al-khurūj means coming forth from graves, as God raises people with water as plants grow.
NAHHAS:v4p221/r17.anchor: مبتدأ وخبره أي الخروج من قبوركم كذا يبعث الله جل وعز ماء

NAHHAS:v4p221/r18.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p221/r18.speaker: أبو إسحاق
NAHHAS:v4p221/r18.claim: Abu Ishaq says God will resurrect you just as He created these things.
NAHHAS:v4p221/r18.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق المعنى كما خلقنا هذه الأشياء نبعثكم

SAMIN-DURR:50:11/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:50:11/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:50:11/r1.claim: رزقا may be a circumstantial accusative meaning “provided for” or “possessing provision.”
SAMIN-DURR:50:11/r1.anchor: يجوز أن يكون حالا أي: مرزوقا للعباد أي: ذا رزق،

SAMIN-DURR:50:11/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:50:11/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:50:11/r2.claim: It may be a verbal noun related to أنبتنا, since this growth is itself provision.
SAMIN-DURR:50:11/r2.anchor: وأن يكون مصدرا من معنى أنبتنا؛ لأن إنبات هذا رزق،

SAMIN-DURR:50:11/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:50:11/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:50:11/r3.claim: It may instead be a purpose accusative.

SAMIN-DURR:50:11/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:50:11/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:50:11/r4.claim: للعباد may be an adjective, attach to the verbal noun, or be its object with an extra lām.
SAMIN-DURR:50:11/r4.anchor: إما صفة، وإما متعلق بالمصدر، وإما مفعول للمصدر

SAMIN-DURR:50:11/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:50:11/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:50:11/r5.claim: به refers to water; ميتا describes بلدة and is masculine because the noun is treated as a place.
SAMIN-DURR:50:11/r5.anchor: أي: بالماء. و " ميتا " صفة ل " بلدة ".

SAMIN-DURR:50:11/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:50:11/r6.speaker: العامة
SAMIN-DURR:50:11/r6.claim: The common reading lightens; Abū Jaʿfar and Khālid read with doubling.
SAMIN-DURR:50:11/r6.anchor: والعامة على التخفيف. وأبو جعفر وخالد بالتثقيل.

ZAJJAJ:v5p43/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p43/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p43/r3.claim: Rizqan has two accusative analyses: a cognate object (“provided them provision”) or a purpose object (“grew these things for sustenance”).
ZAJJAJ:v5p43/r3.anchor: ينتصب على وجهين: أحدهما على معنى رزقناهم رزقا لأن إنباته هذه الأشياء رزق، ويجوز أن يكون مفعولا له، المعنى: فأنبتنا هذه الأشياء للرزق.

ZAJJAJ:v5p43/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p43/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p43/r4.claim: Just as God created these things, He will raise people from the dead.
ZAJJAJ:v5p43/r4.anchor: ثم قال: (كذلك الخروج). أي كما خلقنا هذه الأشياء نبعثكم.

ASAD-NOTES:50:9/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:50:9/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:50:9/r1.claim: Blessed rain makes gardens, grain and clustered dates grow as sustenance for people.
ASAD-NOTES:50:9/r1.anchor: water rich in blessings, and cause thereby gardens to grow, and fields of grain

ASAD-NOTES:50:9/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:50:9/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:50:9/r2.claim: Reviving dead land through rain illustrates how people will come forth from death.
ASAD-NOTES:50:9/r2.anchor: by [all] this We bring dead land to life: [and] even so will be [man's] coming-forth from death

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p442/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p442/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p442/r1.claim: Islahi links the resurrection argument to 17:99: the Creator of heaven and earth has power to create people again.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p442/r1.anchor: Do they not see that the God Who has created the heavens and the earth has power to create their like?

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p442/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p442/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p442/r2.claim: The fuller account in 79:27–33 invokes creation of the sky, earth, water, fodder, and mountains to establish God's power, greatness, wisdom, and providence.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p442/r2.anchor: A deliberation on these verses will show that they contain all the aspects of power, greatness, wisdom and providence

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p442/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p442/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p442/r3.claim: The heavenly and earthly signs display harmony and thereby argue for God's oneness.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p442/r3.anchor: there is found great harmony between the two.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p442/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p442/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p442/r4.claim: The providential benefits of the signs entail that people will face reward and punishment.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p442/r4.anchor: The elements of providence found in them necessitate reward and punishment

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p442/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p442/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p442/r5.claim: Rain reviving barren land makes life after death imaginable, just as dead ground becomes alive after rain.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p442/r5.anchor: the way rain enlivens a barren piece of land also brings the scenario of life after death before a person.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p443/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p443/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p443/r4.claim: The orderly clusters reveal the Creator's lavish power, wisdom, and creativity, while the benefits impose an obligation for which people will be questioned.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p443/r4.anchor: The layered clusters of dates bear witness from their very form that the Creator has so copiously used His power, wisdom and creativity

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p443/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p443/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p443/r5.claim: People will be questioned about the divine favours they received.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p443/r5.anchor: they shall one day be questioned about them.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p443/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p443/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p443/r6.claim: The revival of dead land by rain is the sūrah's central theme and analogizes the resurrection that its rejecters deem impossible.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p443/r6.anchor: Rising of the dead should be regarded analogous to this with which they are being informed of; however, they regard it to be impossible.

NASHR:v2p223/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p223/r6.speaker: أبو جعفر
NASHR:v2p223/r6.claim: Abū Jaʿfar doubles the yāʾ in all the listed forms of «الميتة/ميتا», «بلد ميت», and «الحي من الميت والميت من الحي».
NASHR:v2p223/r6.anchor: فقرأ أبو جعفر بتشديد الياء في جميع ذلك، ووافقه نافع في يس الأرض الميتة

QIRAAT-ER:50:11:8#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:50:11:8#1/r1.speaker: vw
QIRAAT-ER:50:11:8#1/r1.claim: The vw form has doubled yāʾ (mayyitan) rather than contracted maytan; grammarians debate whether mayyit is currently dying and mayt already dead.
QIRAAT-ER:50:11:8#1/r1.anchor: Vowel-length variant: mayyitan (with tashdīd on yāʾ) vs standard maytan

ALUSI-FULL:v26p176#5/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p176#5/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p176#5/r1.claim: رزقا is purposive: God grows plants to provide for His servants; it modifies فأنبتنا.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p176#5/r1.anchor: أي ليرزقهم علة لقوله تعالى : ( فأنبتنا )

ALUSI-FULL:v26p176#5/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p176#5/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p176#5/r2.claim: By placing provision after insight and reminder, the verse signals that reflection should precede and matter more than bodily enjoyment.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p176#5/r2.anchor: الأول بالتبصير والتذكير تنبيه على أن اللائق بالعبد أن يكون انتفاعه

ALUSI-FULL:v26p176#5/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p176#5/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p176#5/r3.claim: Alternatively, رزقا is a cognate verbal noun for أنبتنا, since growing plants is provision, like قعدت جلوسا, or it is a circumstantial “provided for.”
ALUSI-FULL:v26p176#5/r3.anchor: أن يكون ( رزقا ) مصدرا من معنى ( أنبتنا ) لأن الإنبات رزق

ALUSI-FULL:v26p176#5/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p176#5/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p176#5/r4.anchor: وأحيينا به ( أي بذلك الماء ( بلدة ميتا

ALUSI-FULL:v26p176#5/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p176#5/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p176#5/r5.claim: A dead town is barren land without growth, made productive so that it swells and sprouts.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p176#5/r5.anchor: أرضا جدبة لا نماء فيها بأن جعلناها بحيث ربت وأنبتت

ALUSI-FULL:v26p176#5/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p176#5/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p176#5/r6.claim: The masculine adjective agrees with بلدة as understood in the sense of البلد or place.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p176#5/r6.anchor: وتذكير ( ميتا ) لأن البلدة بمعنى البلد والمكان

ALUSI-FULL:v26p176#5/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p176#5/r7.speaker: أبو جعفر، خالد
ALUSI-FULL:v26p176#5/r7.claim: Abu Ja'far and Khalid read ميتا with a strengthened consonant.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p176#5/r7.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر وخالد ( ميتا ) بالتثقيل

ALUSI-FULL:v26p176#5/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p176#5/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p176#5/r8.claim: Fronting كذلك gives emphatic, restrictive focus; ذلك points to the life just described, and its distance suggests its extraordinary rank.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p176#5/r8.anchor: جملة قدم فيها للقصد إلى القصر وذلك إشارة إلى الحياة

ALUSI-FULL:v26p176#5/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p176#5/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p176#5/r9.claim: Resurrection from the graves is like the striking revival of dead land, not something essentially different.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p176#5/r9.anchor: مثل تلك الحياة البديعة حياتكم بالبعث من القبور لا كشيء مخالف لها

ALUSI-FULL:v26p176#5/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p176#5/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p176#5/r10.claim: Calling plant emergence revival and human resurrection خروج magnifies plant growth, makes resurrection seem easy, and clarifies the analogy.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p176#5/r10.anchor: لتوضيح منهاج القياس وتقريبه إلى إفهام الناس

ALUSI-FULL:v26p176#5/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p176#5/r11.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v26p176#5/r11.claim: Al-Zamakhshari takes كذلك as the predicate; al-Alusi says this is the apparent parse, while treating كاف as subject is possible.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p176#5/r11.anchor: على الابتداء و ( الخروج ) خبر ونقل عن الزمخشري أنه قال : ( كذلك ) الخبر وهو الظاهر

ALUSI-FULL:v26p176#5/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p176#5/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p176#5/r12.claim: Making ذلك الخروج a subject-predicate construction with كاف meaning مثل is possible by analogy with أبو يوسف أبو حنيفة, but al-Alusi calls it contrived.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p176#5/r12.anchor: على نحو أبو يوسف أبو حنيفة والكاف واقع موقع مثل

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p357#2/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p357#2/r9.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p357#2/r9.claim: The phrase means that God made these things sustenance for the servants, with the verb understood.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p357#2/r9.anchor: رزقا للعباد} أي جعلناها رزقا للعباد،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p357#2/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p357#2/r10.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p357#2/r10.claim: “By it” refers to the rain; God grows vegetation in a dead town.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p357#2/r10.anchor: وأحيينا به} أي بالمطر، {بلدة ميتا} أنبتنا فيها الكلأ

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p357#2/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p357#2/r11.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p357#2/r11.claim: Just as rain revives the dead land, people will come forth from their graves.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p357#2/r11.anchor: بلدة ميتا} أنبتنا فيها الكلأ {كذلك الخروج} من القبور.

BAYDAWI-FULL:50:11-13/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:50:11-13/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:50:11-13/r1.claim: رزقا is either the purpose of growing plants or a verbal noun, since growth itself is provision.
BAYDAWI-FULL:50:11-13/r1.anchor: علة ل { أنبتنا } أو مصدر، فإن الإنبات رزق

BAYDAWI-FULL:50:11-13/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:50:11-13/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:50:11-13/r2.claim: The land revived by water is barren and has no growth.

BAYDAWI-FULL:50:11-13/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:50:11-13/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:50:11-13/r3.claim: As the land comes alive, people emerge alive after death.
BAYDAWI-FULL:50:11-13/r3.anchor: كما حييت هذه البلدة يكون خروجكم أحياء بعد موتكم

BIQAI-FULL:v7p250/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p250/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p250/r1.claim: After the sign of heaven, the argument turns to earth; heaven is more wondrous and majestic, while familiarity with earth and its fruits makes people overlook its evidence.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p250/r1.anchor: وأخرها لأن السماء أدل على المجد الذي هذا سياقه , لأنها أعجب صنعة وأعلى علوا وأجل مقدارا وأعظم أثرا

BIQAI-FULL:v7p250/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p250/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p250/r7.claim: Because human nature can pull down what reason elevates, a person returning to God may fear rejection; the passage encourages return by describing provision and revival.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p250/r7.anchor: ولما كان الإنسان لما له من النقصان لا يزال كلما أعلاه عقله أسفله طبعه , فكان ربما ظن أنه لا يقبل إذا رجع

BIQAI-FULL:v7p250/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p250/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p250/r8.claim: God provides the fruits as sustenance for His servants.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p250/r8.anchor: ولما كان سكانها لا غنى لهم عن الرزق , قال ممتنا عليهم

BIQAI-FULL:v7p250/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p250/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p250/r9.claim: Rain revives a dead town, just as the dead will emerge from their graves.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p250/r9.anchor: وأحيينا به بلدة ميتا كذلك الخروج

BIQAI-FULL:v7p251/r16.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p251/r16.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p251/r16.claim: God caused these plants to grow because they form part of the provision He assigned to His servants.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p251/r16.anchor: أي أنبتنا به ذلك لأجل أنه بعض ما جعلناه رزقهم

BIQAI-FULL:v7p251/r17.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p251/r17.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p251/r17.claim: The feminine ending in town signals its extreme weakness and need for support and stability.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p251/r17.anchor: وسمها بالتاء إشارة غلىأناه في غاية الضعف والحاجة إلى الثبات والخلو عنه

BIQAI-FULL:v7p251/r18.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p251/r18.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p251/r18.claim: Calling the town dead further stresses how fully dependent it is on revival.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p251/r18.anchor: للزيادة في تقرير تمكن الحاجة فيها

BIQAI-FULL:v7p251/r19.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p251/r19.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p251/r19.claim: Plants emerging from pulverized earth resemble the dead rising from graves, restored as they were in worldly life.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p291/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p291/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p291/r1.claim: After reflection on the heavens and earth, the discourse shifts to recurring cycles of life and death, preparing the proof that resurrection is possible.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p291/r1.anchor: نقل الكلام إلى التذكير بإيجاد آثار من آثار تلك المصنوعات تتجدد على مرور الدهر حية ثم تموت ثم تحيا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p293/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p293/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p293/r2.claim: Provision for the servants is an accusative of purpose, an infinitive meaning so that God may provide and sustain people.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p293/r2.anchor: مفعول لأجله لقوله : { فأنبتنا به جنات } ( ق : 9 ) إلى آخره ، فهو مصدر ، أي لنرزق العباد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p293/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p293/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p293/r3.claim: Servants means people as God's servants; the plural of a human slave is instead abid. The phrase is both an argument and a favor.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p293/r3.anchor: والعباد : الناس وهو جمع عبد بمعنى عبد الله ، فأما العبد المملوك فجمعه العبيد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p293/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p293/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p293/r4.claim: The provision phrase serves as an argument and a reminder of God's favor.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p293/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p293/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p293/r5.claim: The verb We gave life is coordinated with the noun provision, which is derived from a verb; the sense is that God provided people and revived land.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p293/r5.anchor: عطف على { رزقا للعباد } عطف الفعل على الاسم المشتق من الفعل وهو رزقه المشتق لأنه في معنى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p293/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p293/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p293/r6.claim: The land's revival provides pasture for livestock and wild animals, serving as both proof and favor.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p293/r6.anchor: وأحيينا به بلدة ميتا ، أي لرعي الأنعام والوحش فهو استدلال وفيه امتنان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p293/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p293/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p293/r7.claim: A balda is a tract or section of land.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p293/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p293/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p293/r8.claim: The lightly pronounced mayyit is synonymous with the doubled form; 36:33 calls dead land a sign for people.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p293/r8.anchor: والميت بالتخفيف : مرادف الميت بالتشديد قال تعالى :

IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p293/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p293/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p293/r9.claim: The adjective is masculine with the feminine land because it is understood as balad, a synonym, or as makān, its genus.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p293/r9.anchor: وتذكير الميت وهو وصف للبلدة ، وهي مؤنث على تأويله بالبلد لأنه مرادفه ، وبالمكان لأنه جنسه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p293/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p293/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p293/r10.claim: Drought resembles death because signs of life disappear; vegetation is called life, and cultivating and watering barren land is idiomatically called reviving dead land.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p293/r10.anchor: شبه الجدب بالموت في انعدام ظهور الآثار ، ولذلك سمي ضده وهو إنبات الأرض حياة . ويقال لخدمة الأرض اليابسة وسقيها : إحياء موات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p293/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p293/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p293/r11.claim: Creation of these beings from nothing proves resurrection possible: restoring already existing, weaker beings is more feasible and easier.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p293/r11.anchor: لأن خلق تلك المخلوقات من عدم يدل على أن إعادة بعض الموجودات الضعيفة أمكن وأهون

IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p293/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p293/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p293/r12.claim: The final clause summarizes the proof of resurrection and is best treated as a resumption or, for those who allow it, a parenthetical close.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p293/r12.anchor: فهذه الجملة فذلكة للاستدلال على إمكان البعث الذي تضمنته الجمل السابقة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p293/r13.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p293/r13.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p293/r13.claim: The demonstrative points to reviving dead earth: just so God revives people after death and decay, while magnifying the remarkable resurrection.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p293/r13.anchor: والإشارة { بذلك } إلى ما ذكر آنفا من إحياء الأرض بعد موتها ، أي كما أحيينا الأرض بعد موتها كذلك نحيي الناس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p293/r14.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p293/r14.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p293/r14.claim: The definite article marks the known emergence of people from graves; al-khuruj became a conventional name for resurrection, as 70:43 and 50:42 show.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p293/r14.anchor: والتعريف في { الخروج } للعهد ، أي خروج الناس من الأرض كما قال تعالى : { يوم يخرجون من الأجداث سراعا }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p293/r15.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p293/r15.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p293/r15.claim: Putting the prepositional phrase first draws attention to the predicate's rebuttal of impossibility and makes listeners anticipate the subject.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p293/r15.anchor: وتقديم المجرور على المبتدإ للاهتمام بالخبر لما في الخبر من دفع الاستحالة وإظهار التقريب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p157#3/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p157#3/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p157#3/r9.claim: Rizqan is an accusative verbal noun, and the pronoun in bihi refers to the rain.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p157#3/r9.anchor: رزقا نصب على المصدر والضمير في: به عائد على المطر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p157#3/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p157#3/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p157#3/r10.claim: The town is described as dead with an ellipsis understood as rain or land.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p157#3/r10.anchor: ووصف البلدة ب «ميت» على تقدير القطر والبلد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p157#3/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p157#3/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p157#3/r11.claim: Most readers lighten mayyitan; Abū Jaʿfar and Khālid read it with gemination.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p157#3/r11.anchor: وقرأ الناس «ميتا» مخففا، وقرأ أبو جعفر وخالد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p157#3/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p157#3/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p157#3/r12.claim: The signs just mentioned exemplify and prove resurrection; al-khurūj means emerging from the graves.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p157#3/r12.anchor: هذه الآيات كلها إنما هي أمثلة وأدلة على البعث

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p8#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p8#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p8#2/r1.claim: The plants and fruits are produced as provision for people.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p8#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p8#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p8#2/r2.claim: The land is revived by rain.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p8#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p8#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p8#2/r3.claim: In the same way, people will emerge from their graves.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p396#2/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p396#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p396#2/r8.claim: The produce is provision for all creatures.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p396#2/r8.anchor: {رزقا للعباد} أي: للخلق، {وأحيينا به بلدة ميتا}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p396#2/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p396#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p396#2/r9.claim: Rain revives formerly barren land: it swells, stirs, and grows beautiful plants and flowers, becoming green after having no vegetation.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p396#2/r9.anchor: وهي: الأرض التي كانت هامدة، فلما نزل عليها الماء اهتزت وربت وأنبتت من كل زوج بهيج،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p396#2/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p396#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p396#2/r10.claim: The witnessed revival of dead land exemplifies resurrection: God likewise revives the dead, and this visible sign of power is more evident than what resurrection-deniers reject.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p396#2/r10.anchor: فهذا مثال للبعث بعد الموت والهلاك، كذلك يحيي الله الموتى.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p396#2/r11.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p396#2/r11.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p396#2/r11.claim: He supports the resurrection argument by citing that creating the heavens and earth is greater than creating people, that God can revive the dead, and that revived earth is a sign of that power.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p396#2/r11.anchor: كقوله تعالى: {لخلق السموات والأرض أكبر من خلق الناس} [غافر: 57]

BURSEVI:v9p86#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p86#2/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p86#2/r10.claim: The planting is explained as sustenance for God's servants; placing this after the previous verse's signs for reflection teaches that contemplation should take priority over enjoyment of food.
BURSEVI:v9p86#2/r10.anchor: وفي تعليله بذلك بعد تعليل أنبتنا الأول بالتبصرة والتذكرة تنبيه على أن الواجب على العبد

BURSEVI:v9p87/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p87/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p87/r1.claim: The Persian couplet teaches that eating is for living and remembering God, rather than living merely for eating.

BURSEVI:v9p87/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p87/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p87/r2.claim: The earlier verse chiefly demonstrates divine power through the greatest bodies, mentioning growth secondarily, so it suits 'reflection and reminder'; this verse explains their benefits as sustenance, which follows creation.
BURSEVI:v9p87/r2.anchor: المقصود من الآية الأولى هو الاستدلال على القدرة بأعظم الأجرام

BURSEVI:v9p87/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p87/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p87/r4.claim: Maytan is masculine to agree with the implicit masculine noun balad or makān.

BURSEVI:v9p87/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p87/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p87/r5.claim: God revives barren land by making it swell and grow plants and flowers, so it moves after having been still and lifeless.
BURSEVI:v9p87/r5.anchor: بأن جعلنا بحيث ربت وأنبتت أنواع النبات والأزهار فصارت تهتز بها

BURSEVI:v9p87/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p87/r6.speaker: أبو هريرة
BURSEVI:v9p87/r6.claim: Abū Hurayra reports that when rain came and gutters flowed, the Prophet would say, 'No famine upon you this year.' No grading is given.
BURSEVI:v9p87/r6.anchor: روي أبو هريرة رضي الله عنه قال : كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

BURSEVI:v9p87/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p87/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p87/r7.claim: The predicate is advanced to restrict the comparison: resurrection from graves is like the wondrous life rain brings to land, with nothing in that resurrection unlike it.
BURSEVI:v9p87/r7.anchor: جملة قدم فيها الخبر للقصد الى القصر

BURSEVI:v9p87/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p87/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p87/r8.claim: A report says God sends rain for forty nights, which enters the earth like male seed; flesh, veins, and bones grow, then God revives people and brings them out.
BURSEVI:v9p87/r8.anchor: وقد روي أن الله يمطر السماء أربعين ليلة كمني الرجال يدخل في الأرض

BURSEVI:v9p87/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p87/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p87/r9.claim: Calling the emergence of plants 'revival' and resurrection 'emergence' magnifies vegetation's renewal, makes resurrection seem less difficult, and clarifies their correspondence for people.
BURSEVI:v9p87/r9.anchor: وفي التعبير عن إخراج النبات من الأرض بالإحياء عن حياة الموتى بالخروج تفخيم لشأن الانبات

BURSEVI:v9p87/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p87/r10.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v9p87/r10.claim: Al-Kāshifī says that reflection on a buried seed's revival and emergence after concealment can lead one to infer the revival of the dead.
BURSEVI:v9p87/r10.anchor: قال الكاشفي : واكر كسى تأمل كند

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p385#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p385#2/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p385#2/r6.claim: Rizqan may mean We grew them as provision, since growing entails provision, or be a purpose clause: We grew them to provide for people.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p385#2/r6.anchor: رزقا } على أنبتناها رزقا ، لأن الإنبات في معنى الرزق

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p385#2/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p385#2/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p385#2/r7.claim: Just as God revives this dead land, He will bring people to life after death.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p385#2/r7.anchor: كذالك الخروج } كما حييت هذه البلدة الميتة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p385#2/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p385#2/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p385#2/r8.claim: The kāf in thus is nominative as the subject of an equative clause.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p385#2/r8.anchor: والكاف في محل الرفع على الابتداء

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p343/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p343/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p343/r7.claim: Provision is blessed rain and what it produces: plants, harvested grain, and clustered palm fruit.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p343/r7.anchor: يعني ما أنزله من السماء من ماء مبارك , وما أخرجه من الأرض

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p343/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p343/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p343/r8.claim: The dead town proves resurrection: re-creating what had a source is easier than first creation, and reviving dead plants shows God can restore people for recompense.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p343/r8.anchor: جعل هذا كله دليلا على البعث والنشور من وجهين : أحدهما

MUQATIL:50:11/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:50:11/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:50:11/r1.claim: Rain revives barren land without vegetation, which then grows; this whole provision is for God's servants.
MUQATIL:50:11/r1.anchor: { وأحيينا به } بالماء { بلدة ميتا } لم يكن عليها نبت فنبتت الأرض

MUQATIL:50:11/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:50:11/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:50:11/r2.claim: People will likewise emerge from their graves through water, as plants emerge from earth through water.
MUQATIL:50:11/r2.anchor: { كذلك الخروج } [آية: 11] يقول: وهكذا تخرجون من القبور بالماء، كما أخرجت النبت من الأرض بالماء

MUQATIL:50:11/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:50:11/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:50:11/r3.claim: The signs of rain and growth make people recognize God's oneness and power to resurrect.
MUQATIL:50:11/r3.anchor: ليعرفوا توحيد الرب وقدرته على البعث

NASAFI-FULL:v4p171#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p171#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p171#2/r1.claim: Rizqan means We grew the crops as provision, either a verbal noun not formed from the verb anbatnā or a purpose object meaning We grew them to feed people.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p171#2/r1.anchor: اى انبتناها رزقا للعباد لان الانبات في معنى الرزق فيكون رزقا مصدرا من غير لفظة أو هو مفعول له

NASAFI-FULL:v4p171#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p171#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p171#2/r2.claim: By that water God revived a town whose vegetation had dried up.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p171#2/r2.anchor: ﴿ وأحيينا به ﴾ بذلك الماء ﴿ بلدة ميتا ﴾ قد جف نباتها

NASAFI-FULL:v4p171#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p171#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p171#2/r3.claim: People will likewise emerge alive after death: reviving dead land resembles reviving the dead.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p171#2/r3.anchor: اى كما حييت هذه البلدة الميتة كذلك تخرجون احياء بعد موتكم لان احياء الموات كاحياء الاموات

NASAFI-FULL:v4p171#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p171#2/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p171#2/r4.claim: The kāf is nominative as the subject.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p171#2/r4.anchor: والكاف في محل الرفع على الابتداء

QURTUBI-FULL:50:10-11/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:50:10-11/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:50:10-11/r6.claim: Rizqan can be an object with an implied “We provided,” a complement of the planting understood as provision, or a purpose expression; provision is what is made ready for use.
QURTUBI-FULL:50:10-11/r6.anchor: أي رزقناهم رزقا، أو على معنى أنبتناها رزقا لأن الإنبات في معنى الرزق،

QURTUBI-FULL:50:10-11/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:50:10-11/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:50:10-11/r7.claim: As God revives dead land by rain, He will bring people alive from their graves; the resurrection is likened to the land's revival.
QURTUBI-FULL:50:10-11/r7.anchor: أي من القبور أي كما أحيا الله هذه الأرض الميتة فكذلك يخرجكم أحياء بعد موتكم

QURTUBI-FULL:50:10-11/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:50:10-11/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:50:10-11/r8.claim: The kāf in kathālika is in the predicate position of an initial clause; maytan is masculine because the intended referent is the place, though maytatan would also be valid.
QURTUBI-FULL:50:10-11/r8.anchor: فالكاف في محل رفع على الابتداء. وقد مضى هذا المعنى في غير موضع. وقال «ميتا» لأن المقصود المكان ولو قال ميتة لجاز.

RAZI-FULL:v28p136#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p136#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p136#2/r1.claim: Rizqan is accusative either as a cognate accusative, since growing the plants is provision, or as a purpose accusative, since they are grown to provide for people.
RAZI-FULL:v28p136#2/r1.anchor: فكأنه تعالى قال : أنبتناها إنباتا للعباد

RAZI-FULL:v28p136#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p136#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p136#2/r2.claim: One explanation is that the heavens and earth point to creation and resurrection, while fruits as provision point to continued sustenance after resurrection; the passage separates these proofs by beginning the water-and-growth discussion afterward.
RAZI-FULL:v28p136#2/r2.anchor: فكأن الأول تبصرة وتذكرة بالخلق ، والثاني تذكرة بالبقاء بالرزق

RAZI-FULL:v28p136#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p136#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p136#2/r3.claim: A second explanation names the obvious benefit of fruit as provision, while the sky's role in providing sustenance is less obvious to people, though it is the source of provision by God's decree and has other benefits.
RAZI-FULL:v28p136#2/r3.anchor: ثانيها : أن منفعة الثمار الظاهرة هي الرزق فذكرها ومنفعة السماء الظاهرة ليست أمرا عائدا إلى انتفاع العباد

RAZI-FULL:v28p136#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p136#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p136#2/r4.claim: A third explanation says “provision” stresses God's beneficence, making the deniers' rejection especially reprehensible as denial of their benefactor.
RAZI-FULL:v28p136#2/r4.anchor: ثالثها : قوله { رزقا } إشارة إلى كونه منعما لكون تكذيبهم في غاية القبح فإنه يكون إشارة ( للتكذيب ) بالمنعم

RAZI-FULL:v28p136#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p136#3/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p136#3/r1.claim: The earlier proof is for every penitent servant, but provision reaches all; the penitent eats gratefully and remembers God, while others eat like livestock.
RAZI-FULL:v28p136#3/r1.anchor: لأن الرزق حصل لكل أحد ، غير أن المنيب يأكل ذاكرا شاكرا للإنعام ، وغيره يأكل كما تأكل الأنعام

RAZI-FULL:v28p136#3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p136#3/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p136#3/r3.claim: “We revived with it a dead land” is coordinated with “We grew by it” in the preceding verse.
RAZI-FULL:v28p136#3/r3.anchor: ثم قال تعالى : { وأحيينا به بلدة ميتا } عطفا على { أنبتنا * به } ( ق: 9 )

RAZI-FULL:v28p136#3/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p136#3/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p136#3/r4.claim: If crop growth shows sustenance after resurrection, reviving dead land also proves resurrection; it follows the provision evidence because the heavens and earth already established resurrection, before the passage returns to this proof.
RAZI-FULL:v28p136#3/r4.anchor: قوله { وأحيينا به } إشارة إلى أنه دليل على الإعادة كما أنه دليل على البقاء ، ويدل عليه قوله تعالى : { كذالك الخروج }

RAZI-FULL:v28p136#3/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p136#3/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p136#3/r5.claim: Alternatively, reviving land means water greens it and produces flowers, a more widespread adornment than crops; although greenery comes first, crops and fruit are mentioned first as the greater blessing.
RAZI-FULL:v28p136#3/r5.anchor: الإحياء غير إنبات الرزق لأن بإنزال الماء من السماء يخضر وجه الأرض ويخرج منها أنواع من الأزهار ولا يتغذى به ولا يقتات

RAZI-FULL:v28p137/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p137/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p137/r1.claim: The feminine marker may be present or omitted with mayyit because it is a lightened form of mayyit, and faʿīl as an active adjective can take feminine marking.
RAZI-FULL:v28p137/r1.anchor: جاز إثبات التاء في الميت وحذفها عند وصف المؤنث بها ، لأن الميت تخفيف للميت ، والميت فيعل بمعنى فاعل

RAZI-FULL:v28p137/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p137/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p137/r2.claim: Faʿīl does not mark gender here because distinguishing agent from patient matters more than distinguishing masculine from feminine patients; faʿīl serves both active and passive senses without a distinguishing letter, unlike mafʿūl.
RAZI-FULL:v28p137/r2.anchor: الحاجة إلى التمييز بين الفاعل والمفعول أشد من الحاجة إلى التمييز المفعول المذكر والمفعول المؤنث

RAZI-FULL:v28p137/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p137/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p137/r3.claim: Rāzī explains the feminine suffix in “the dead earth” at 36:33 because earth is described as an agent, whereas “dead town” omits it because the town's underlying state is life; he compares “a good town” at 34:15, where the active sense is clear and the suffix appears.
RAZI-FULL:v28p137/r3.anchor: الأرض أراد بها الوصف فقال : { الأرض الميتة } لأن معنى الفاعلية ظاهر هناك

RAZI-FULL:v28p138/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p138/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p138/r1.claim: The dead emerge at resurrection as plants emerge when rain revives a dead land: the earth splits and they come out.
RAZI-FULL:v28p138/r1.anchor: تشققت وخرج منها النبات كذلك تشقق ويخرج منها الأموات

RAZI-FULL:v28p138/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p138/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p138/r2.claim: The wording supports reading الرجْع in 50:3 as return (intransitive): if they denied extraction, the fitting answer would have said إخراج, but it says خروج.
RAZI-FULL:v28p138/r2.anchor: لأنه تعالى بين لهم ما استبعدوه فلو استبعدوا الرجع الذي هو من المتعدي لناسب أن يقول

RAZI-FULL:v28p138/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p138/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p138/r3.claim: Alternatively, extraction and خروج are cause and effect: denying the cause entails denying the effect, so God emphatically affirms the effect after they denied both.
RAZI-FULL:v28p138/r3.anchor: ووجهها هو أن الرجع والإخراج كالسبب

STUDYQURAN:50:6/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:50:6/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:50:6/r1.claim: The passage calls people to reflect on nature’s beauty, order, and bounty as signs of Divine Mercy, wisdom, and Resurrection.
STUDYQURAN:50:6/r1.anchor: This is one of several passages to call human beings to reflect upon the beauty, proportionality, and bounty of the natural world

STUDYQURAN:50:6/r13.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:50:6/r13.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:50:6/r13.claim: Provision refers to the waters, gardens, grain, and date palms just mentioned.
STUDYQURAN:50:6/r13.anchor: As provision for His servants refers to the waters, gardens, grain, and date palms in the previous verses

STUDYQURAN:50:6/r14.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:50:6/r14.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:50:6/r14.claim: God revives dead land with the rainwater, as elsewhere stated.
STUDYQURAN:50:6/r14.anchor: God revives a dead land with the water that is sent down, as in 16:65

STUDYQURAN:50:6/r15.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:50:6/r15.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:50:6/r15.claim: Coming forth means Resurrection; just as God created the preceding provisions, He will bring forth all humans and jinn.
STUDYQURAN:50:6/r15.anchor: The coming forth refers to the Resurrection

STUDYQURAN:50:6/r16.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:50:6/r16.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:50:6/r16.claim: The revival of earth can also symbolize God reviving spiritually dead hearts.
STUDYQURAN:50:6/r16.anchor: the revival of the earth can also be taken as a reference to the manner in which God revives the hearts of those who are spiritually dead

TABATABAI:50:1-4/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:50:1-4/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:50:1-4/r2.claim: It then recalls God's knowledge and power through creation of the adorned heavens, spread and planted earth, and rain that provides for and revives creation.
TABATABAI:50:1-4/r2.anchor: وتنبه ثانيا على علمه وقدرته تعالى بالإشارة إلى ما جرى من تدبيره تعالى في خلق السماوات

TABATABAI:50:9-14/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:50:9-14/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:50:9-14/r4.claim: Sustenance is that by which life is maintained.

TABATABAI:50:9-14/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:50:9-14/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:50:9-14/r5.claim: The phrase is an object of purpose: God produced the gardens, grain, and palms to provide sustenance for His servants.
TABATABAI:50:9-14/r5.anchor: مفعول له أي أنبتنا هذه الجنات

TABATABAI:50:9-14/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:50:9-14/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:50:9-14/r6.claim: The elaborate provision of these plants displays vast planning and inexhaustible knowledge and power; reviving people remains easy even if their bodily particles disperse.
TABATABAI:50:9-14/r6.anchor: فمن خلق هذه النباتات ليرزق به العباد بما في ذلك من التدبير الوسيع الذي يدهش اللب ويحير العقل

TABATABAI:50:9-14/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:50:9-14/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:50:9-14/r7.claim: The revived town supplies a second proof of resurrection: something’s possibility is shown by an analogous event, dead plants emerging from dead earth.
TABATABAI:50:9-14/r7.anchor: من مسلك إثبات إمكان الشيء بوقوع مثله

TABATABAI:50:9-14/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:50:9-14/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:50:9-14/r8.claim: This proof differs from the prior argument from God’s knowledge and power; it infers resurrection from the observable revival of the earth.
TABATABAI:50:9-14/r8.anchor: فإن البيان السابق في رد استبعادهم للبعث مستندين

TABRISI:50:11/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:50:11/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:50:11/r1.claim: God made the plants and other growths provisions for His servants; all provision is from God, by His direct act or by causing it, though people may idiomatically be said to provide for others.
TABRISI:50:11/r1.anchor: وكل رزق فهو من الله تعالى بأن يكون قد فعله أو فعل سببه

TABRISI:50:11/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:50:11/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:50:11/r2.claim: The water sent from heaven revives a barren, drought-stricken land that had grown nothing.
TABRISI:50:11/r2.anchor: أي بذلك الماء الذي أنزلناه من السماء

TABRISI:50:11/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:50:11/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:50:11/r3.claim: As God brings dead land to life with water, He will bring the dead out of their graves; power over either act entails power over the other.
TABRISI:50:11/r3.anchor: مثل ما أحيينا هذه الأرض الميتة بالماء نحيي الموتى يوم القيامة فيخرجون من قبورهم

TABRISI:50:11/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:50:11/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:50:11/r4.claim: People doubt resurrection because they regularly see rain revive land but have no customary experience of dead humans returning; reflection shows both acts are within God's power.
TABRISI:50:11/r4.anchor: رأوا العادة مستمرة في إحياء الموات من الأرض بنزول المطر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p387/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p387/r1.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p387/r1.claim: Abu Ishaq parses rizqan either as an implied cognate object, “We provided them provision,” or as a purpose object, “We brought forth these things for provision.”
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p387/r1.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: ينتصب على وجهين: أحدهما: على معنى رزقناهم رزقا,

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p387/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p387/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p387/r2.claim: The emergence from graves is like the creation of plants; God likewise brings the dead out, as in 7:57.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p387/r2.anchor: أي من القبور. والمعنى: كما خلقنا هذه الأشياء نبعثكم كقوله: {كذلك نخرج الموتى}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p387/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p387/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p387/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says rain falls like men's seminal fluid and flesh and bones grow upon the dead.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p387/r3.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: ينزل من السماء مطر كنطف الرجال تنبت عليهم اللحوم والعظام

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p387/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p387/r4.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p387/r4.claim: Muqatil compares people emerging from their graves through rain to plants emerging from earth through rain.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p387/r4.anchor: وهذا معنى قول مقاتل: يخرجون من القبور بالماء، كما أخرجنا النبت من الأرض بالماء

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:50:5-11/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:50:5-11/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:50:5-11/r7.claim: God provides these things as sustenance for His servants.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:50:5-11/r7.anchor: رزقا للعباد } أي: آتينا هذه الأشياء للرزق { وأحيينا به } بذلك الماء

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:50:5-11/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:50:5-11/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:50:5-11/r8.claim: God revives a dead land with rain just as people will emerge from their graves.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:50:5-11/r8.anchor: وأحيينا به } بذلك الماء { بلدة ميتا كذلك الخروج } من القبور.

ELMALILI:50:6-15/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:50:6-15/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:50:6-15/r17.claim: The crops and dates are brought forth as provision for God’s servants.

ELMALILI:50:6-15/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:50:6-15/r18.speaker: author
ELMALILI:50:6-15/r18.claim: Rain restores life to barren, dry ground whose growth had ceased.
ELMALILI:50:6-15/r18.anchor: bir beldeyi ölmüş iken onunla -o su ile- diriltmekteyiz. Neşv ü nemâdan kesilmiş kuru toprağa hayat vermekteyiz.

ELMALILI:50:6-15/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:50:6-15/r19.speaker: author
ELMALILI:50:6-15/r19.claim: Resurrection from graves is like a dead town revived by rain and is no less within God’s power.
ELMALILI:50:6-15/r19.anchor: İşte hurûc böyledir. Yani ölü bir beldenin bir su indirmekle dirilmesi gibidir. Allah’ın indireceği feyizle sizin de dirilip çıkmanız

ELMALILI:50:6-15/r20.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:50:6-15/r20.speaker: Ebussuud
ELMALILI:50:6-15/r20.claim: Abu al-Suʿud says calling plant emergence ihyāʾ and resurrection khurūj magnifies planting, makes resurrection seem easy, and clarifies their likeness.
ELMALILI:50:6-15/r20.anchor: Ebussuud’un beyânına göre yerden nebâtâtın çıkarılmasına “ihyâ” ve ölülerin dirilmesine “hurûc” tâbir olunması ehemmiyetsiz gibi görülen inbâtın şânını büyütmek

ELMALILI:50:6-15/r21.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:50:6-15/r21.speaker: author
ELMALILI:50:6-15/r21.claim: Elmalılı also reads an allusion to Islam’s emergence and victory through divine favor, bringing new life from a dead community.
ELMALILI:50:6-15/r21.anchor: Her hâlde biz bununla ölmüş bir kavimden feyz-i Hak ile İslâm’ın zuhur ve yeni bir hayat ile ağyara karşı hurûc

MAJAZ:v2p223/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p223/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p223/r1.claim: Al-khurūj refers to the Day of Resurrection; al-ʿAjjāj’s verse calls it the day of rising.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:50:1/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:50:1/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:50:1/r1.claim: The passage addresses monotheism, prophethood, and the afterlife; against denials of resurrection it directs people to God's knowledge and power, the first creation, and the blessings around them.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:50:1/r1.anchor: Hz. Peygamber’in Kur’an (vahiy) yoluyla alıp tebliğ ettiği inanç esasları içinde en önemlileri; bir tek Allah’a kulluk (tevhid), peygamberliğe iman (nübüvvet), öldükten sonra dirilmeye

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:50:1/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:50:1/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:50:1/r2.claim: The resurrection argument is that the God who brought all things from nothing can recreate them, and that He knows exactly what remains or decays in a body, so restoring its like and returning its soul is easy for Him.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:50:1/r2.anchor: Kur’an’ın bu şüpheye karşı ileri sürdüğü delilin iki önemli unsuru vardır

BURHAN:v3p333/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p333/r4.speaker: ابن الزبير
BURHAN:v3p333/r4.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr treats Qaf's move from denial of resurrection to visible signs in the sky and revived land as a comparable shift; these undeniable signs lead to the conclusion that resurrection will likewise occur.
BURHAN:v3p333/r4.anchor: وألحق به الأستاذ أبو جعفر بن الزبير

BURHAN:v3p333/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p333/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p333/r5.claim: After leaving the disbelievers' challenge unanswered and describing the heavens and rain as observable facts they could not deny, God concludes: “Thus is the emergence.”
BURHAN:v3p333/r5.anchor: وذكر اختلافهم المسبب عن تكذيبهم في قوله

BURHAN:v3p358/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p358/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p358/r5.claim: The masculine adjective ميتا is licensed because بلدة is construed as مکان, ‘place’; otherwise it would be feminine.

QUSHAYRI:v3p226/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p226/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p226/r7.claim: Just as God sends water to revive dry land, He can gather people for resurrection; raising the dead is no more difficult than reviving the land.
QUSHAYRI:v3p226/r7.anchor: وكما سقنا هذا الماء إلى بلدة جف نباتها ، وكما فعلنا كل هذه الأشياء ونحن قادرون على ذلك
